questions.q: What does usermod -aG developers jsmith do, and why does the -a flag matter?
options: Creates a brand new group called developers automatically
Adds jsmith to the developers group while keeping their existing group memberships — without -a, those other memberships are silently removed
Deletes the jsmith user account entirely
questions.explain: The -a flag appends the new group rather than replacing jsmith's full set of group memberships.

questions.q: Given the permission string rwxr-xr--, what can "everyone else" (not the owner or group) do with this file?
questions.explain: The final triplet, r--, grants only read permission to everyone outside the owner and group.

questions.q: What octal number represents the permission rwx?
questions.explain: r (4) + w (2) + x (1) adds up to 7, which is why chmod 7xx grants full rwx to the owner.

questions.q: What does chown jsmith:developers file.txt actually change?
options: The user and group that own file.txt
questions.explain: chown changes ownership — who the owner and group columns refer to — which is what the rwx triplets are checked against.

questions.q: Why do production servers typically use sudo instead of letting administrators log in directly as root?
options: sudo makes commands run faster than they would as root
sudo lets an authorized user run one privileged command at a time, logged, instead of granting unrestricted root access for an entire session
There is no real difference between sudo and a root login
sudo is required because root accounts are disabled by default on all Linux distros
questions.explain: sudo creates a per-command audit trail and limits the blast radius of a mistake, instead of leaving someone logged in with unrestricted root access.
